name: Drill-Abyssal
description: Drill-Abyssal is named for the extraordinary vertical tunnels that pierce its ocean floor, geothermal boreholes of natural origin that extend hundreds of kilometers into the planetary crust like the work of some immense drill. Superheated water jets upward through these tunnels, creating towering columns of turbulence that reach from the abyssal depths to the surface, where they erupt as permanent warm geysers surrounded by rings of thriving marine life. The dense atmosphere presses down on a global ocean that never stops churning.

The ocean is warm, turbid, and alive. Bioluminescent organisms of extraordinary variety fill the water column, creating shifting curtains of light visible from orbit. The perpetual storm systems that circle the equator are fed by the thermal energy of the geyser fields, their lightning illuminating the ocean surface in strobing flashes that reveal the shadows of enormous creatures moving just below. The air is thick with salt spray and the organic tang of a hyper-productive ecosystem that has been evolving for billions of years.

A derelict space station tumbles in a slowly decaying orbit, its registry wiped and its origin unknown. More notably, a well-organized pirate operation has established a hidden base within one of the larger geyser rings, using the thermal interference and electromagnetic noise to mask their presence from orbital scans. The pirates have made themselves part of the local economy, trading in biological specimens harvested from the deep tunnels and offering safe harbor to those who ask no questions.

Drill-Abyssal's biological resources are immensely valuable, but the pirate presence has made legitimate research difficult. The fauna inhabiting the geothermal tunnels include species found nowhere else, adapted to crushing pressure and scalding temperatures, with biochemistries that could revolutionize medicine and materials science. Navy patrols have been increased, but the planet's electromagnetic interference and the pirates' intimate knowledge of the geyser fields have made enforcement a frustrating exercise in futility.
